issue.title: GeoIP processor failures will block data ingestion

body:
The `ignore_missing` parameter is about ignoring the error if the field defined by the `field` parameter (`client.ip` in this case) cannot be found.

I agree that allowing to ignore a missing databases (by not adding `tags`) should be possible. I just wonder whether that should be done by the current `ignore_missing` parameter or perhaps via a new parameter (`ignore_missing_database`?). So that the `tags` field isn't added to a document if database is missing.

@martijnvg [the docs](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/geoip-processor.html) for `ignore_missing` state

> If true and field does not exist, the processor quietly exits without modifying the document

This is not being upheld in the example above: the first document, which lacks `client.ip`, is being modified.

It may also be useful to have a separate flag to disable the `tags` addition in case of errors, but I still think either the behaviour of `ignore_missing` needs to change, or the docs do.

> This is not being upheld in the example above: the first document, which lacks client.ip, is being modified.

I overlooked that 2 documents were provided in the simulate api. 
I agree, that the first document shouldn't have the `tags` field.

If database is missing then respect ignore_missing parameter configured on the geoip processor.
If ignore_missing is enabled then the document should not be tagged. In this case the document
shouldn't be tagged.

Closes #87345

issue.title: Revisit decision to use strict mappings
issue.body:
In our well-defined metrics data streams, we currently specify strict mappings. e.g. `metrics-apm.internal-*`:

https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/blob/f61db13498b1ab6af88d5993d4b2c04f6501d65f/apmpackage/apm/data_stream/internal_metrics/manifest.yml#L8-L10

The reason for doing so is that we are (ostensibly) in full control of the mappings, and there should never be any additional fields. We occasionally introduce bugs that invalidate this and lead to users having a bad time, e.g. https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/issues/10773. Other times we find issues with ingest pipelines that unexpectedly and unintentionally introduce fields, e.g. https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/87345. The latter kind of issue is what strict mappings are supposed to surface.

Blocking ingestion is an extreme response to unexpected fields. On the other hand we should not allow dynamic mapping, as that may also lead to documents being rejected, e.g. due to mapping conflicts. We should consider setting `dynamic: false` or `dynamic: runtime`.

body: This is (still? again?) a problem in 8.13.0-SNAPSHOT. I suspect it's due to the [DatabaseUnavailableProcessor](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/e1fe7f48babafa56a422a9289fe1d21bc9174a94/modules/ingest-geoip/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/ingest/geoip/GeoIpProcessor.java#L564), which tags documents indiscriminately.
